title: Felon Sent to Prison for More Than Four Years for  Illegally Possessing a Gun
body: Press Release Felon Sent to Prison for More Than Four Years for  Illegally Possessing a Gun Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Iowa A man who illegally possessed a gun after multiple felony convictions was sentenced today to more than four years in federal prison. Tyrecas Rakeem Matlock, age 35, from Waterloo, Iowa, received the prison term after an April 30, 2026, guilty plea to possession of a firearm by a felon. At the guilty plea, Matlock admitted he possessed a Taurus 9mm caliber pistol after being convicted of multiple prior felonies including possession of marijuana with intent to deliver and possession of a firearm by a felon. Matlock was sentenced in Cedar Rapids by United States District Court Chief Judge C.J. Williams.  Matlock was sentenced to 57 months’ imprisonment.  He must also serve a three-year term of supervised release after the prison term.  There is no parole in the federal system. This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Matlock is being held in the United States Marshal’s custody until he can be transported to a federal prison. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Dillan Edwards and investigated by the Floyd County Sheriff’s Office.  Court file information at https://ecf.iand.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/login.pl . title: Federal grand jury indicts fourteen defendants in $370 million nationwide bank account takeover conspiracy
body: Press Release Federal grand jury indicts fourteen defendants in $370 million nationwide bank account takeover conspiracy Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas Ringleader attempted to flee U.S. before arrest at JFK airport gate DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould today announced that a federal grand jury indicted fourteen defendants, including allegedly corrupt insiders at major banking and telecommunication institutions, for allegedly orchestrating a sweeping nationwide bank‑account‑takeover conspiracy that targeted victims across the U.S. Muhamed Dieye, 35, of Dallas, known to associates by several aliases including “MJ,” “JayJay,” “Medici,” and “Lambomotion Tony,” is the leader and chief architect of the alleged conspiracy. Dieye and the thirteen co-defendants are charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and bank fraud, bank fraud, wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. A federal grand jury returned the 22-count indictment on Aug. 26. It was unsealed today after the arrest of Terrence Dudley a/k/a Willy Watkins, Brian Faceman in Florida, a key co-conspirator in the case. In addition to Dieye and Dudley, the indictment also charges: Maurice Rashad McDuffie, a/k/a Heavvvy Motion Saad Nashat Botros, a/k/a Felix Saucedo , Wesley Swipes , Wesley Swipes Sammed Kweku Okyne, a/k/a OKC , Paris Jawn Renaldo Santez Gaines, a/k/a BlackMigo , OsamaCapone , OsamaBin57 Alphonso Brndon Seke‑Horton, a/k/a The Wizard 302 Terry Leon Daniels Jr., a/k/a onedayrealsoon , Teazy Daniels Jamel Allen Small, a/k/a Paypawerk Kemar Fitzroy Needham, a/k/a Swap King Fx , kingzmanfx Kevin Brandon Flores Cazares, a/k/a John First B , First B (Call) Dylon Amari Ruby, a/k/a slimeyluhdude , AT&T Courtney Jane Sutton C.S. “North Texas is the financial services hub of America, and protecting Main Street families and investors is a top priority of this office,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “These defendants are charged with targeting the life savings of thousands of Americans, and the ringleader was stopped at the gate before he could flee. Target Main Street and we will pursue you with every tool available." A sophisticated, multi‑state identity‑theft ring According to the indictment, Dieye possessed a spreadsheet that contained detailed personal and business information for nearly 3,000 individual victims who collectively held over $373,000,000 across their bank accounts. From July 2023 through November 2024, the defendants allegedly conspired to obtain personal identifying information, produced and trafficked counterfeit identification documents, impersonated victims, manipulated victims’ phone lines by spoofing and SIM swapping, intercepted security codes and used corrupt insiders within banks and telecommunications companies to bypass authentication measures. Among the plays detailed in the indictment, the conspirators allegedly: Accessed or withdrew funds from victim accounts at Truist Bank, Bank of America, First Bank, Woodforest National Bank, JPMorgan Chase Bank, and Charles Schwab Conducted or attempted numerous fraudulent financial transactions, including an attempted $2,000,000 wire to the Emirates Islamic Bank Leveraged aliases referencing violent extremists and organized‑crime figures—such as OsamaCapone and OsamaBin57 —while executing and coordinating complex fraud plays Ringleader attempted to flee the United States Federal law enforcement, working closely with the U.S. Attorney’s Office, arrested Dieye after he allegedly attempted to flee the country. According to the government’s motion to revoke release: Dieye and his family vacated his Dallas residence, shipped most of his possessions to Kenya and traveled with his family to New York to board a one-way flight to Malaysia. Within hours of his flight, the U.S. Attorney’s Office and Diplomatic Security Service secured an arrest warrant. After scanning his boarding pass, Dieye allegedly physically resisted arrest, attempted to destroy one of his cell phones containing evidence that he was researching how to buy a home in Malaysia, and had to be subdued by multiple federal agents. While a Magistrate Court in the Eastern District of New York initially ordered Dieye released on bond, the United States immediately sought and obtained an emergency stay of his release. Dieye has since been transported to the Northern District of Texas, where he and several of his co-defendants remain in federal custody pending trial. If convicted, the defendants face a maximum penalty of 30 years in federal prison on the bank fraud conspiracy charge and 20 years in federal prison on the wire fraud conspiracy charge. Aggravated identity theft carries a mandatory sentence of two years’ imprisonment, consecutive to any other sentence imposed. The Diplomatic Security Service conducted the investigation with substantial assistance from the U.S. Secret Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Homeland Security Investigations, Drug Enforcement Administration, Customs and Border Protection, Social Security Administration Office of Inspector General, Federal Bureau of Investigation, National Insurance Crime Bureau, U.S. Embassy Dakar Senegal Office of Overseas Criminal Investigations, the Dallas Police Department, the Plano Police Department and the Collin County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael J. Murtha from the Major Crimes Section is prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation of criminal conduct, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. title: Former St. Louis Building Inspector Sentenced to 6 Years in Prison for $1.6 Million Fraud
body: Press Release Former St. Louis Building Inspector Sentenced to 6 Years in Prison for $1.6 Million Fraud Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Missouri ST. LOUIS – U.S. District Judge Zachary M. Bluestone on Tuesday sentenced a former City of St. Louis building inspector to six years in prison and ordered him to repay the $1.64 million he stole from programs meant to repair decrepit buildings in St. Louis. Adebanjo “Banjo” Popoola, 58, was a building division inspector with the City of St. Louis and was responsible for managing important aspects of two programs designed to help stabilize and rehabilitate city properties, Stable Communities STL and Prop NS. In in a sentencing memo, Assistant U.S. Attorney Hal Goldsmith wrote, “This is a case of greed, plain and simple." Popoola “abused his longstanding and substantial position of trust with the City of St. Louis in order to enrich himself and his family members.” Popoola “destroyed two well-intentioned local and federal funded programs meant to stabilize decaying and debilitating properties within the City,” Goldsmith said. Stable Communities STL was funded through federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds and intended for privately-owned properties. Prop NS was intended for residential properties owned by the City’s Land Reutilization Authority (LRA) and was funded through general obligation bonds. Popoola was primarily responsible for identifying properties for rehab or stabilization; developing the scope of work; seeking, reviewing and awarding bids; inspecting the work that had purportedly been completed on each property and certifying that the work had been completed so funds could be disbursed to the contractors. Popoola steered 41 contracts to Farst Construction LLC, a company he helped organize with his sister, a nurse living in Texas with no background or experience in construction. He directed 50 contracts to Premier Finish Contractors LLC, a company he helped his fiancée organize. Popoola “was so bold as to give 42% of the total funds disbursed under the City’s Stable Communities STL program to his sister’s and his wife’s companies,” Goldsmith wrote. Popoola concealed his role in the companies from the city and his sister and his fiancée (later wife) concealed their connection to Popoola. On multiple projects, Farst and Premier failed to perform the rehabilitation and stabilization work for which the companies were paid but Popoola falsely certified that the work had been performed completely and properly. Popoola and his family members reaped $1,642,908 from the scheme. Popoola spent the stolen money on residential mortgage payments, multiple vehicle purchases and repairs, travel expenses, his September 2023 wedding in Hawaii, casino gambling and other dining and entertainment expenses. The owner of a building on Rowan Avenue in the Hamilton heights neighborhood wrote in a victim impact statement to the court that Popoola’s theft of $48,500 in repair funds left a building “with severe, unaddressed structural decay that was actively masked by fraudulent building inspection reports… imposing an immense, unexpected financial burden on me as an independent developer.” St. Louis Mayor Cara Spencer said in her own statement that the city may have to return millions of dollars in ARPA funds because of Popoola’s crimes. Innocent contractors were harmed when the city froze payments during the investigation, which also halted other stabilization work, including buildings damaged by the May 2025 tornado. Popoola, 57, pleaded guilty in June in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to three counts of wire fraud. “As a building inspector, Banjo Popoola stole more than $1.64 million in taxpayer dollars intended to stabilize and rebuild St. Louis neighborhoods. While families were left living next to deteriorating and unsafe buildings, he diverted those funds to finance his Hawaiian wedding, pay his mortgage, and cover personal expenses,” said Special Agent in Charge Chris Crocker of the FBI St. Louis Division. “The damage caused by this kind of corruption extends far beyond the theft of taxpayer money. When building inspectors compromise their responsibility to enforce safety standards for personal financial gain, they put entire communities and the lives of those residents at risk.” The FBI investigated the case, with substantial cooperation from the City of St. Louis Comptroller’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Hal Goldsmith prosecuted the case. Contact Robert Patrick, Public Affairs Officer, robert.patrick@usdoj.gov. Updated November 3, 2026 Topics Financial Fraud Public Corruption Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Missouri, Eastern

title: Federal Indictment Charges Adams Morgan Club Owner in Methamphetamine Trafficking
body: Press Release Federal Indictment Charges Adams Morgan Club Owner in Methamphetamine Trafficking Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON – A two-count Indictment unsealed today in U.S. District Court charges Aman Mehari Weldemariam, 34, of the District of Columbia, with two counts of unlawful distribution and possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “Methamphetamine destroys lives, fuels crime, and threatens the safety of our communities,” said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “As alleged, the defendant distributed large quantities of this dangerous drug while operating businesses in the heart of the District. We are committed to aggressively prosecuting drug traffickers and protecting the District from those who put profit ahead of public safety.” Weldemariam owns the Green Island Café and Club Heaven and Hell in Adams Morgan. He was arrested this morning outside a residential apartment building in Northeast Washington, D.C., where he was in possession of a kilogram of suspected cocaine powder. Law enforcement recovered from his residence a fully loaded firearm and approximately 140 Suboxone strips.  Law enforcement also searched his businesses and recovered an additional 200 Suboxone strips, a digital scale, and narcotics packaging material. Weldemariam made his first appearance this afternoon before U.S. Magistrate Judge Moxila A. Upadhyaya. He is being held pending his Wednesday detention hearing. The Indictment alleges that on July 16, 2026, Weldemariam distributed more than 500 grams of methamphetamine. The Indictment also alleges that on Aug. 3, 2026, Weldemariam additionally distributed more than 500 grams of methamphetamine. Weldemariam allegedly distributed a total of nearly eight pounds of methamphetamine in controlled sales.  Weldemariam was on probation at the time of the offenses for a prior 2017 drug-related conviction in Fairfax County and a 2020 drug-related conviction in Richmond County. This case is being investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration and the Stafford County Sheriff’s Office. The matter is being prosecuted by the Violent Crime and Narcotics Trafficking Section of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia. weldemariam_indictment_certified.pdf 26cr251 Updated November 3, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - District of Columbia

title: Four-Time Convicted Felon Sentenced to More than 10 Years in Prison for Illegal Possession of Multiple Firearms
body: Press Release Four-Time Convicted Felon Sentenced to More than 10 Years in Prison for Illegal Possession of Multiple Firearms Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Alabama BIRMINGHAM, Ala.  – A convicted felon has been sentenced for illegal possession of multiple firearms, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr. U.S. District Court Judge Anna M. Manasco sentenced Timothy Shane Postell, 40, of Bessemer, Alabama, to 130 months in prison.  Postell pleaded guilty to being a felon in possession of a firearm in two separate and unrelated cases. According to the plea agreements, Postell illegally possessed firearms on two separate occasions. On April 16, 2022, an officer with the Leeds Police Department responded to a call at a retail store in Leeds.  The officer arrived on the scene and found a female and Postell on a couch, and both appeared to be under the influence of narcotics.  They were arrested for public intoxication. The officer searched Postell and recovered a stolen pair of tennis shoes, narcotics, and a loaded SCCY 9mm pistol. On February 7, 2026, an officer with the Hueytown Police Department initiated a traffic stop on a vehicle driven by Postell. As the officer approached the vehicle, Postell fled the scene recklessly—speeding and passing vehicles with oncoming traffic and in no-passing zones. The pursuit continued until Postell stopped at the end of a dirt road. Postell exited the vehicle and ran. An officer deployed his taser with no effect but eventually got close enough to tackle Postell and handcuff him.  The officer searched Postell and recovered a loaded Canik 9mm pistol from one of Postell’s inside jacket pockets and a loaded Glock 10mm pistol from the other inside jacket pocket. During a search of Postell’s vehicle, officers recovered a loaded Marlin .22 rifle, body armor plates, methamphetamine, and drug paraphernalia. “Keeping firearms out of the hands of convicted felons is critical in protecting our communities,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. “This defendant repeatedly demonstrated disregard for the law. This 130-month sentence sends a clear message that illegal firearm possession by repeat offenders will have serious consequences. We are grateful to our law enforcement partners for their dedication and continued efforts to keep our communities safe.” “ATF prioritizes public safety and is committed to bringing individuals who unlawfully possess firearms to justice” said ATF Special Agent in Charge James VanVliet.  “Mr. Postell, a four-time convicted felon, showed a pattern of criminal behavior in this case, illegally possessing firearms in multiple incidents. ATF will continue to work with our state and local law enforcement partners to make our communities safe by pursuing, apprehending, and prosecuting such individuals who demonstrate a propensity for lawlessness and recklessness.” Postell is prohibited from possessing firearms because of his four prior felony convictions that span from 2007 to 2021.  Postell was convicted in the Superior Court of Paulding County, Georgia in February 2007, of Robbery by Intimidation, Theft by Taking, and Aggravated Assault and in September 2013, of Possession of Cocaine; in the Circuit Court of Jefferson County, Alabama in May 2014 for Robbery, Second Degree; and in the District Court of Shelby County, Alabama in February 2021, of Burglary, Third Degree. The ATF investigated the case along with the Leeds Police Department and Hueytown Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney Darius C. Greene prosecuted the case. Updated November 3, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Alabama, Northern

title: McKinley County Man Pleads Guilty to Assaulting Woman
body: Press Release McKinley County Man Pleads Guilty to Assaulting Woman Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A McKinley County man pleaded guilty to assaulting a woman after offering her a ride in his car, then driving her toward a remote residence and repeatedly groping her along the way, despite her repeatedly ordering him to stop. According to court documents, on March 23, 2026, Barton Rico Cooeyate , 41, offered the victim a ride while she was walking along a road within the exterior boundaries of the Zuni Pueblo. After the victim accepted, Cooeyate suggested they drive to a location in Vanderwagen, New Mexico. Instead, Cooeyate drove past the turnoff and headed toward a rural residence approximately 15 miles away. During the drive, Cooeyate repeatedly touched the victim’s breasts and thighs over her clothing and attempted to kiss her despite her telling him she did not want to be touched. The victim ultimately escaped Cooeyate ’s car and hid until a Zuni Pueblo Tribal Ranger stopped Cooeyate for an unrelated DWI investigation. The victim suffered injuries, including a contusion to her left forearm. Cooeyate pleaded guilty to Assault with Intent to Commit Any Felony. At sentencing, Cooeyate faces up to 10 years in prison, to be followed by up to three years of supervised release. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today. The Gallup Resident Agency of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case with assistance from the Zuni Fish and Wildlife and the Zuni Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Zachary C. Jones is prosecuting the case. Updated November 3, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - New Mexico Press Release Number: 26-299

title: Dubuque Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for COVID-19 Related Unemployment Fraud
body: Press Release Dubuque Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for COVID-19 Related Unemployment Fraud Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Iowa A man who stole government funds intended to aid unemployed workers during the COVID-19 pandemic was sentenced on October 28, 2026, to more than two years in federal prison.  Jacob Michael Laufenberg, age 36, from Dubuque, Iowa, received the prison term after a February 23, 2026, guilty plea to wire fraud. Information from the guilty plea and sentencing hearings showed that in May 2020, Laufenberg applied for unemployment benefits in Iowa.  He subsequently received unemployment benefits until April 2021.  While he was receiving unemployment benefits, he concealed his employment with two employers and the fact that he was incarcerated in a county jail for nearly two months.  Laufenberg’s false statements about his employment and custody status caused him to receive unemployment funds to which he was not entitled. Laufenberg was sentenced in Cedar Rapids by United States District Court Chief Judge C.J. Williams.  Laufenberg was sentenced to 33 months’ imprisonment.  He was ordered to make $17,102 in restitution to Iowa Workforce Development.  He must also serve a five-year term of supervised release after the prison term.  There is no parole in the federal system. Laufenberg is being held in the United States Marshal’s custody until he can be transported to a federal prison. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars.  Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Kyndra Lundquist and investigated by the United States Department of Labor, Office of Inspector General. Court file information at https://ecf.iand.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/login.pl .  The case file number is 25-CR-1040. Follow us on X @USAO_NDIA. Updated November 3, 2026 Topics COVID-Related Fraud Financial Fraud Component USAO - Iowa, Northern

title: Grandfather and Grandson Charged in Early Morning Armed Robbery, Kidnapping, Carjacking Crime Spree
body: Press Release Grandfather and Grandson Charged in Early Morning Armed Robbery, Kidnapping, Carjacking Crime Spree Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Missouri KANSAS CITY, Mo. – Two Kansas City, Kan., men were charged in an eighteen-count indictment by a federal grand jury for their roles in an early morning March 25, 2026, violent crime spree involving several victims. Following their initial appearances in federal court, Michael T. Lomax, 57, and Mario O. Lomax, 19, were charged with multiple federal crimes including: conspiracy to commit Hobbs Act Robbery, conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, Hobbs Act Robbery, discharging/brandishing/using firearms during and in relation to crimes of violence, carjacking, and other related offenses.  Both men had initially been charged in Jackson County, Missouri Circuit Court. That case was dismissed in favor of federal charges. According to the probable cause statement, two men wearing dark clothing, facemasks, and armed with handguns stormed into the house of 63-year-old Victim #1 at 6:20 a.m. Victim #1 was ordered on the floor at gunpoint to direct the men to any money or guns inside the residence. Victim #1 was then forced around their home at gunpoint, with the defendants discharging their firearms at least once for their compliance. Victim #1 was forced into their basement and told to remain there while they fled the residence. The defendants stole U.S. Currency, firearms, Victim #1’s car keys, and their cell phone. While fleeing the area, the defendants came upon a Chevy Silverado, sitting in the driveway of a home, with the engine idling. The adult owner of the Silverado, Victim #3, was outside of the vehicle assisting one of their children.  Sitting in the backseat of the Silverado was their other child, a juvenile, Victim #2.  The two defendants got into the front driver and passenger seats of the vehicle, noticed the child in the backseat, then pointed their handguns at them while telling the child to get out of the vehicle. Victim #2 got out of the vehicle and the defendants fled in the Silverado. In taking the Silverado, the defendants also stole Victim #3’s cell phones, bag, and medication. Using surveillance video, witness statements, witness identification, GPS, and numerous other investigative tools, Michael T. Lomax and Mario O. Lomax were identified as the assailants from the morning of March 25, 2026. The charges contained in the indictment are simply accusations, and not evidence of guilt. Evidence supporting the charges must be presented to a federal trial jury, whose duty is to determine guilt or innocence. Under federal statutes, both Michael T. Lomax and Mario O. Lomax are currently subject to a minimum sentence of 24 years imprisonment, with a maximum sentence of up to life in federal prison without parole. The minimum and maximum statutory sentences are prescribed by Congress and are provided here for informational purposes only. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jeffrey Q. McCarther and Kelly Collins. It was investigated by the Kansas City, Missouri Police Department. Project Safe Neighborhoods Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . Updated November 3, 2026 Topic Project Safe Neighborhoods Component USAO - Missouri, Western

title: Former Missouri Postal Worker Admits Stealing Rebates, Receipts from the U.S. Mail
body: Press Release Former Missouri Postal Worker Admits Stealing Rebates, Receipts from the U.S. Mail Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Missouri CAPE GIRARDEAU – A former postal worker in Poplar Bluff on Tuesday admitted stealing Menards rebate checks and store receipts that were mailed in for rebates. Ron Harty, 44, pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court in Cape Girardeau to one count of theft of mail by a postal employee and one count of possession of stolen mail. On August 15, 2025, Hart purchased a fire pit and 110 patio blocks from the home improvement store Menards using rebate checks from four victims totaling $280.95. He also used a $64.05 rebate check in his own name, 88% of which came from five victims who mailed receipts to Menards seeking rebates only to have their mail intercepted by Harty. An investigation revealed six other victims who sent in nine receipts that Harty intercepted. Harty worked at the Poplar Bluff Post Office in Butler County as the lead sales and service associate at the time, as well as at the Williamsville Post Office in Wayne County. Harty, of Butler County, is scheduled to be sentenced on Feb. 9, 2027. Each charge carries a potential penalty of up to five years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000 or both prison and a fine. The U.S. Postal Inspection Service investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Chris Shelton is prosecuting the case. Contact Robert Patrick, Public Affairs Officer, robert.patrick@usdoj.gov. Updated November 3, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - Missouri, Eastern

title: Former Berkeley County Sheriff’s Office Employee Admits Guilt in Multi-Million-Dollar Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Former Berkeley County Sheriff’s Office Employee Admits Guilt in Multi-Million-Dollar Fraud Scheme Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of West Virginia MARTINSBURG, WEST VIRGINIA – A former employee of the Berkeley County Sheriff’s Office has admitted her role in a years‑long fraud and embezzlement scheme that targeted vulnerable individuals and public funds, U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey announced today. Lisa Lee French, 48, of Martinsburg, admitted that between 2007 and October 2024, she conspired to steal cash payments collected by the Sheriff’s Office and to manipulate conservatorship and estate accounts overseen by the office. French acknowledged issuing fraudulent checks, forging signatures, misusing a sheriff’s signature stamp, and diverting funds for her personal benefit. “Fraud on this scale harms not only those directly targeted, but the entire Berkeley County community. We are committed to ensuring accountability and protecting the integrity of our public offices,” said U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey. The victims include Berkeley County taxpayers, individuals under conservatorship, and the Berkeley County Sheriff’s Office itself. According to court documents, the scheme involved more than 700 fraudulent transactions, over 550 of them forged checks, connected to at least 59 conservator bank accounts. In total, the fraud amounted to nearly $3 million. French has agreed to pay $2,737,932 in restitution to the identified victims. A second defendant, Barbara Gail Gooden, is awaiting trial on March 23, 2027. Read the original press release here . Senior Litigation Counsel Andrew Cogar is prosecuting the case. The investigation was conducted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Berkeley County Sheriff’s Office, and the West Virginia State Auditor’s Office. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the formation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”), which focuses on investigating and prosecuting fraud against the American public. This effort supports the President’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole‑of‑government initiative chaired by the Vice President to address fraud, waste, and abuse in federal benefit programs. U.S. Magistrate Judge Robert W. Trumble presided. Updated November 3, 2026 Topic Fraud Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - West Virginia, Northern

title: Regulators explore credit union reforms to support growth, innovation and better outcomes for members
body:
Regulators explore credit union reforms to support growth, innovation and better outcomes for members | Bank of England – the UK's central bank Our use of cookies We use necessary cookies to make our site work. We’d also like to use some non-essential cookies (including third-party cookies) to help us improve the site. By clicking ‘Accept recommended settings’ on this banner, you accept our use of analytics cookies.   For more information on how these cookies work please see our Cookie policy . Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Regulators explore credit union reforms to support growth, innovation and better outcomes for members Credit unions could benefit from several ideas put forward today by the Prudential Regulation Authority and Financial Conduct Authority aimed at helping the sector grow, innovate and meet the changing needs of their members. Published on  
        03 November 2026 News release Credit unions could benefit from several ideas put forward today by the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) aimed at helping the sector grow, innovate and meet the changing needs of their members. Credit unions, which are member-owned and typically focus on savings and personal loans in a specific occupation, community or area, have over two million members in the UK. Building on the joint PRA and FCA 2025 Mutuals Landscape report, this discussion paper examines whether the regulatory framework remains proportionate as the sector evolves, and explores how credit unions can expand access to financial services and improve outcomes for the members they serve. Options the regulators are seeking views on include: Removing some requirements on internal audit and regulatory documents for smaller credit unions, cutting red tape without compromising stability; Creating a risk-based framework for larger, more complex credit unions, giving them more flexible capital requirements; Applying relevant rules for smaller deposit takers, such as the standardised approach for risk weighted assets, to replace the current simple leverage ratio they report on; Applying a simplified version of the Basel framework, streamlining capital add-ons for large credit unions with specific exposures, and applying a simple capital buffer for absorbing shocks in stress periods; What barriers there are to credit unions offering new products and services, including how shared-service organisations and third-party organisations can best support investment, technology and operational capability; Giving credit unions additional guidance on FCA expectations around working with third-parties to provide important services; Whether changes to FCA fees could reduce regulatory costs and support sustainable growth; Providing credit unions a path to convert into building societies, bringing the benefits of a framework more tailored to specific lending and a wider range of funding tools; Reviewing the current framework for solvent exit, providing further flexibility to transfer business or restructure in an orderly manner. Shoib Khan, Director of UK Deposit Takers at the Prudential Regulation Authority, said: “Credit unions are a vital part of our financial services sector, and we have scope to make their regime even more proportionate and growth-friendly. We want to have an open, transparent dialogue with firms, and I look forward to seeing their honest feedback.” Sheree Howard, Executive Director of Authorisations at the Financial Conduct Authority, said: “Credit unions provide valuable support to millions of members, including many who may otherwise struggle to access affordable financial services. As the sector evolves, it is important that the regulatory framework keeps pace, enabling credit unions to innovate, grow and meet the changing needs of their members while continuing to deliver good outcomes for consumers. We want to hear directly from the sector about what is working well, where barriers remain, and how the regulatory framework may need to adapt to support a strong, sustainable future for credit unions.” The regulators are encouraging firms to offer their feedback on the options presented and whether there are other options which have not been included. The possibilities at this stage give more options to firms with very different business models, growth trajectories and risk profiles. Notes to editors Read the full Discussion Paper . Today’s announcement builds on a joint report released by the regulators on the wider mutuals sector, which outlined measures to support the sector’s growth and resilience. title: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
body: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI From infrastructure planning and transportation to public services, cities are using NVIDIA-powered applications to address local needs and expand capacity for the broader AI ecosystem. November 2, 2026 by Esther Lee 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge. Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used. Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin , NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own. Agentic AI for Cities From resident services to vision agents, cities are adopting NVIDIA agentic AI to deliver faster, more responsive public services. City teams don’t need a massive infrastructure investment to get started building these AI services: depending on the workload, NVIDIA RTX workstations or a small GPU system may be enough. In Spain, 1MillionBot combines open source ALIA models trained at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center with NVIDIA Nemotron and other models in resident-service agents for Madrid Digital (Comunidad de Madrid), Administració Oberta de Catalunya and 150+ deployments across Spain, handling municipal procedures, appointment requests, urban-planning incidents and service inquiries. In the San Francisco Bay Area , LiveX is bringing its AI City vision to life with NVIDIA Cosmos world models and Nemotron open models, and Omniverse and Metropolis libraries on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs. The interactive, conversational AI hosts understand people’s needs, provide answers and take action, and can be tailored to local languages and service needs in airports, hospitals, local events and other public spaces. Vision AI agents can turn existing city camera feeds into operational insights, helping teams identify mobility and safety issues and coordinate emergency responses across city services. In Wrocław, Poland , K2K is building shared AI infrastructure using NVIDIA accelerated computing, NVIDIA Cosmos world reasoning models, and NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) to transform existing camera streams into actionable intelligence for mobility, safety and event response — using the same infrastructure across several city functions. In Malaysia , ITMAX bundles infrastructure and agentic AI applications into long-term managed services for cities, including for traffic management. Built with reference to Cosmos, Nemotron and the Metropolis VSS blueprint, ITMAX’s SamurAI V2 vision agents are scaling on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs to support 17,000+ cameras by 2027. ITMAX integrates TeraSim, an open source traffic simulation platform from Laplace Intelligence , to test signal timing, reducing peak-hour corridor travel times by up to 26%. Plan and Operate Critical Infrastructure With Digital Twins Beyond public-facing services, digital twins can help cities expedite infrastructure planning, minimizing disruption to local communities. City digital twins can also serve as a real-time operational simulation to facilitate faster decision-making. At Dangote’s Lekki refinery in Nigeria, Honeywell Technologies’ Forge Plant Cognition uses Nemotron-powered AI agents to understand operational data. A digital twin of the plant and its processes, built using Omniverse libraries, is also planned to support simulation and training. The platform, built on Dell PowerEdge servers with NVIDIA RTX PRO accelerators, helps operators identify bottlenecks, anticipate equipment and process issues, and optimize plant performance. In Taiwan , Linker Vision and Dutch architecture firm MVRDV are using NVIDIA Omniverse and Nemotron to build environmental, social and governance agents that can assess the environmental impact of various urban planning scenarios, simulating 15-year outcomes of an urban forest canopy in 10 minutes — increasing design iteration speed from two weeks per iteration to less than an hour. Build a Broader Local AI Ecosystem Cities can extend AI to more services by building on infrastructure already in place and adding capacity. Shared resources and managed services can help extend those capabilities across departments and municipalities. At Morocco’s Tanger Med port, Cires Technologies is expanding a sovereign AI factory for planned applications in worker safety, congestion analysis, cargo routing and port operations. Cires Technologies is also building an ecosystem of application providers to develop local models and applications for ports and cities. Beyond city services, Barcelona Supercomputing Center’s AI Factory Accelerator Programme gives startups access to sovereign computing, technical support and training. BSC AI Factory also supports research and innovation for startups — spanning agriculture, medical imaging, knowledge access and speech services. Learn how NVIDIA and its ecosystem are bringing physical AI, agentic AI and local AI factories to cities worldwide at Smart City Expo World Congress, running Nov. 3-5 in Barcelona, where NVIDIA Vice President of EMEA Paolo Guglielmini will deliver a keynote address followed by a panel moderated by Charbel Aoun, director of smart city and spaces for EMEA at NVIDIA. title: Advancing research and partnering with universities in Singapore
body: Advancing research and partnering with universities in Singapore Nov 03, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Along with a new research hub in Singapore, Google is deepening its academic partnerships in the country with more than $6 million in grants for NUS and NTU — driving breakthroughs in AI for science and compute efficiency, strengthening AI safety frameworks, and nurturing scientific leaders. Yossi Matias Vice President, Google and General Manager, Google Research Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary We are providing new research grants to universities in Singapore to support scientific discovery. This funding helps researchers study Alzheimer’s disease, improve computing efficiency, and build safer artificial intelligence systems. By investing in these local institutions, we are helping students and scientists develop the tools needed to solve complex global problems. You can expect these partnerships to foster new breakthroughs in medicine, technology, and human well-being. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Technology is already transforming how we approach the world’s toughest challenges, and continuing that momentum requires supporting the people driving foundational science. With our newly established research hub in Singapore , and as we continue to scale existing health research initiatives in the country — including bringing open models like MedGemma to frontline care settings — Google is also deepening its academic partnerships in Singapore by investing over $6 million in new research grants and capacity-building initiatives at National University of Singapore (NUS) and Nanyang Technological University (NTU). Backing foundational and applied breakthroughs Our targeted grants address both urgent biomedical frontiers and the core building blocks of computing: Alzheimer’s research ($1.5 million grant — NUS) : Selected from over 3,500 global applications, NUS has been awarded an AI for Science Google.org Impact Challenge Grant to advance breakthroughs in neurodegenerative disease research using AI models and data science. Computing efficiency and regional languages ($500,000 grant — NUS) : This funding supports machine learning efficiency — focusing on sustainable compute and model serving optimization — and regional language processing. AI safety and security ($340,000 grant — NTU) : We are funding four sponsored research studies at NTU focused on advancing AI safety frameworks, robust evaluation methodologies, trustworthy multi-agent systems, and privacy-preserving LLM watermarking. The Google team met with NUS leadership, including Senior Vice Provost Prof. Bernard Tan and Dean of Computing Prof. Tulika Mitra, to align on new research infrastructure and cross-disciplinary workstreams. Building capacity for research ecosystem and future scholars Beyond individual research projects, true ecosystem enablement requires investing in long-term institutional infrastructure and talent pipelines. At NTU, a $750,000 AI for Science Capacity Fund Grant will help build permanent research capabilities across Southeast Asia. Under Professor Ho Teck Hua’s regional academic leadership, this initiative will establish lasting infrastructure, foster internal research agents, and build ethical AI frameworks that elevate the region’s scientific capacity. Google.org and Google DeepMind are also providing $3 million in funding to support INSEAD’s Thrive Lab in Singapore, which aims to advance global research into how people and organizations can thrive alongside rapid technological change. The lab will explore how education, workplaces, and communities can better support people to develop skills, find purpose, and build meaningful relationships in a changing world. This human-centered research sits alongside a broader wave of scientific breakthroughs driving the region forward. Whether unlocking insights into neurodegenerative diseases, making models more efficient and inclusive of local languages, or establishing safe research infrastructure, Singapore’s academic community continues to set a global benchmark for innovation. We are proud to enable with our tools and models the faculty, researchers, and students who are not just experimenting with AI, but preparing to lead the next era of scientific progress The Google team met with the NTU Deputy President & Provost, Prof Christian Wolfrum and colleagues to discuss partnerships across frontier research and AI safety, science, and education. title: Treasury Announces Marketable Borrowing Estimates
body: November 2, 2026 Sources and Uses Table WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury today announced its current estimates of privately-held net marketable borrowing for the October–December 2026 and January–March 2027 quarters. During the October–December 2026 quarter, Treasury expects to borrow $618 billion in privately-held net marketable debt, assuming an end-of-December cash balance of $850 billion. The borrowing estimate is $10 billion lower than announced in August 2026, primarily due to the higher-than-assumed beginning of quarter cash balance, partially offset by lower projected net cash flows. Excluding the higher-than-assumed beginning-of-quarter cash balance, the current quarter borrowing estimate is $24 billion higher than announced in August. During the January–March 2027 quarter, Treasury expects to borrow $800 billion in privately-held net marketable debt, assuming an end-of-March cash balance of $1.000 trillion. During the July–September 2026 quarter, Treasury borrowed $742 billion in privately-held net marketable debt and ended the quarter with a cash balance of $984 billion. In August 2026, Treasury estimated borrowing of $739 billion and assumed an end-of-September cash balance of $950 billion. The $4 billion in higher privately-held net marketable borrowing resulted primarily from the higher-than-assumed end-of-quarter cash balance, offset by higher net cash flows. Excluding the higher-than-assumed end-of-quarter cash balance, actual borrowing was $30 billion lower than announced in August. Additional financing details relating to Treasury’s Quarterly Refunding will be released at 8:30 a.m. on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. ### 1. Privately-held net marketable borrowing excludes rollovers (auction “add-ons”) of Treasury securities held in the SOMA but includes financing required due to SOMA redemptions. Secondary market purchases of Treasury securities by SOMA do not directly change privately-held net marketable borrowing but, all else equal, when the securities mature and assuming the Federal Reserve does not redeem any maturing securities, would increase the amount of cash raised for a given privately-held auction size by increasing the SOMA “add-on” amount. Additionally, buybacks are not expected to significantly affect privately-held net marketable borrowing as new issuance replaces securities that are bought back. 2. title: Economy Statement for the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee
body: November 2, 2026 Introduction The economy under the Trump Administration is strong, supported by robust business investment in equipment and intellectual property products, as well as solid household consumption growth. Business fixed investment (BFI) rose by over 10% at an annual rate over the first three quarters of 2026, driven by investments in new equipment and intellectual property. Since December 2025, the private sector has added 634,000 net new jobs across a broadening range of industries. The unemployment rate and initial unemployment claims remain low, and real weekly wages have grown since the President’s inauguration. Real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) The economy in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q26) grew at the fastest pace in the last four quarters. According to the advance estimate, real GDP grew by 3.4% at an annual rate, accelerating sharply from the 2.2% advance in 2Q26. Core demand in the private sector remained unusually strong, with private domestic final purchases (PDFP) – the combination of PCE, BFI, and residential investment – rising 4.9% at an annual rate, the strongest pace in over five years and following a 4.6% gain in 2Q. Apart from outsized growth of PDFP in the recovery from the short pandemic recession, these were the first back-to-back gains above 4.5% since 2014. The robust PDFP growth in 2Q and 3Q26 suggests a marked boost in the economy’s already-solid capacity for self-sustaining growth in future quarters. BFI grew by 12.7% at an annual rate in 3Q26 – after the very rapid paces of 9.0% in 2Q and 9.9% in 1Q26 – and alone contributed 1.8 percentage points to GDP growth. The third quarter’s rate was the fastest in 15 years, outside of wide swings seen during the pandemic. Equipment investment surged by 20.9% at an annual rate, the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, bringing the annualized rate thus far in 2026 to 16.6%.  While super intelligence-related (SI-related) investments contributed to record levels of equipment capital expenditure through the first three quarters, capital expenditure growth was broad-based in 3Q26. Industrial equipment investment rose at an annual rate of 24.7%, following 27.0% annualized growth in 2Q26. Investment in intellectual property products expanded by 8.4% at an annual rate, reflecting businesses’ continued high levels of investment in software, as well as research and development. Structures investment turned strongly positive in 3Q26, rising 5.4% at an annual rate, after inching up 0.1% in the previous quarter. Structures investment in 3Q26 was the strongest since 4Q23, and this quarter marked the first back-to-back quarterly gains in structures investment in three years. Spending on data centers accelerated to a triple-digit pace in 3Q26. Persistently strong personal consumption expenditures (PCE), which account for roughly two-thirds of the U.S. economy, remained the largest contributor to GDP growth. PCE grew by 3.8% at an annual rate in 3Q26, matching the 2Q pace and adding 2.5 percentage points to real GDP growth. Consumer spending on services accelerated in 3Q26 (led by both health care services and food services and accommodations), while goods spending remained solid (led by prescription drugs). Residential investment declined by 3.3% at an annual rate, reversing a 2.8% increase in 2Q.  The decrease in residential investment shaved 0.1 percentage points from growth.  Spending on single-family structures and brokers’ commissions (the latter related to existing home sales) both declined, more than offsetting a slight increase in multifamily structures investment. Of the remaining components of GDP, the trade deficit widened, posing a larger drag on growth. Exports of goods and services declined, led by petroleum and related products—though exports of intellectual property services increased at a double-digit rate. Meanwhile, imports surged, largely due to non-automotive capital goods. These imports are enabling U.S. businesses to meet the increased demand arising from a boom in capital expenditures. On balance, net exports subtracted 3.3 percentage points from GDP growth. By contrast, the change in private inventories and total government spending both added to economic growth. The federal contribution to growth surged, reflecting more national defense expenditures as well as less drawdown in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Meanwhile, state and local government expenditures were essentially flat. Public spending and the change in private inventories added a combined 2.5 percentage points to real GDP growth in 3Q26. Labor Markets Job growth remained consistent with breakeven employment in 3Q26, and other measures of labor markets remained healthy (see Table 2 – Labor Market Indicators). Private-sector employment growth and the unemployment rate indicate a full-employment economy—one that has steady job growth with neither rising unemployment nor inflationary pressures from wages. The prime-age (ages 25 to 54) labor force participation rate (LFPR) remained at a high level despite a slight decline in the overall LFPR. Job openings were relatively stable in both absolute terms and relative to the number of unemployed persons. Preliminary 4Q26 readings indicate that unemployment claims through mid-October stand near multi-decade lows. Net new payrolls averaged 51,000 per month in 3Q26. Year to date, establishments have added an average of 68,000 jobs per month in 2026. The private sector continues to lead job growth, and payroll job creation has begun to broaden across various sectors. In 3Q26, average job growth in the private sector was 54,000 per month, slowing from 79,000 per month in 2Q26. For the first time since early 2023, health and education services accounted for less than half of private-sector job growth and manufacturers, wholesale traders, and transportation and warehousing firms saw solid net employment growth. Government payrolls declined slightly in 3Q26, shedding an average of 4,000 jobs per month that was largely due to local governments. Total federal payrolls continued to hold at about 2.68 million workers, down from 3.01 million in January 2025. The unemployment rate declined further in 3Q26 to an average of 4.1%—down from averages of 4.3% in the first half of the year. This is well in line with mainstream estimates of the noncyclical unemployment rate—that is, consistent with stable inflation and steady economic growth. Wage growth remained solid in the third quarter: over the year through September 2026, nominal average hourly earnings (AHE) for all employees were up 3.0%, and average weekly earnings were up 3.6% over this period. The difference between AHE and AWE growth reflects a small increase in average weekly work hours. The Employment Cost Index (ECI) for all private workers, which controls for compositional changes and includes employee benefits, rose 3.4% over the year ending in September 2026.  This was a tick faster than Q2’s pace, reflecting stable wage growth and slightly faster increase in employee benefits. Labor force participation declined slightly in 3Q26, partly reflecting ongoing demographic pressures. The overall LFPR slipped to an average of 61.6% in 3Q26 from 61.7% in 2Q26. Although the LFPR among prime-age workers ticked down in 3Q26 to 83.5%, it remained 0.4 percentage points above the previous business cycle peak in January 2020. Participation remains particularly resilient among prime-age men: the LFPR for this group averaged 89.3% in 3Q26, just 0.1 percentage point shy of the previous business cycle peak. Monthly job openings averaged 7.2 million in July and August (latest data available), down 0.2 million from 2Q but up from 6.9 million per month in 4Q25 and 1Q26. The ratio of job openings to unemployed persons averaged 1.0 per month in July and August. Other indicators reflect labor markets’ ongoing health and stability. The layoff rate remains stable and near historical lows and the hires rate has remained stable since mid-2024. Initial unemployment claims trended down in 3Q26 and remained exceptionally low by historical standards through mid-October. Business applications reached a record high of more than 576,000 in July and remained high through Q3, indicating potential increases in new firm births and associated opportunities for American entrepreneurs. Inflation Headline CPI rose 3.7% over the 12 months through September 2026, picking up from the 3.0% annual CPI inflation rate through September 2025. Energy inflation drove roughly 40% of the increase. Average headline inflation ticked up to 0.4% per month in 3Q26 from 0.2% in 2Q26 (see Table 3 – Inflation Indicators). Energy price inflation accelerated in 3Q26. CPI inflation for energy goods and services averaged 1.9% per month in 3Q26, up from the monthly average of 0.6% in 2Q26 but well below the 3.2% monthly average in 1Q26. Food price inflation averaged 0.1% per month in 3Q, down from 0.3% in 2Q, as pressures in the food-at-home category – including beef and coffee prices – receded. Over the 12 months through September, food price inflation was 2.5%, 0.6 percentage points below its year-earlier rate. Twelve-month core CPI inflation, which excludes the volatile components of food and energy, stood at 2.6% as of September, slowing from the 3.0% rate through September 2025. On a monthly average basis, core inflation ticked up to 0.3% in 3Q26 after averaging 0.2% per month in the first and second quarters. Monthly core goods prices increased 0.2% on average in 3Q26, after declining by 0.1% per month in 2Q26. About half of the swing was attributable to new and used motor vehicles, which had flipped from a deflationary to an inflationary force beginning in 2Q. Nonetheless, on a twelve-month basis, core goods inflation was 0.7% through September 2026, the slowest rate since June 2025. Rent of housing inflation decelerated to 0.3% per month in 3Q26, down from 0.4% in 2Q26. Rent of housing inflation was 3.2% over the year through September, well below the 3.7% year-earlier rate and slightly below the pre-pandemic average of 3.3%. Inflation for rent of housing services (rent of primary residence and owners’ equivalent rent) has eased since 2024. After slowing by half in 2Q26, inflation for non-housing core services averaged 0.4% per month in 3Q26. Most of the acceleration of non-housing core services was due to a pickup in transportation services. Over the year through September 2026, non-housing core services inflation was 3.1%, slowing slightly from the 3.2% year-earlier rate. The PCE price index has notable differences in weights and methodologies versus the CPI. Over the past 20 years, twelve-month CPI inflation has exceeded PCE inflation by about 0.35 percentage points on average. Over the year through September 2026, headline PCE inflation was 3.6%, above the 2.8% pace over the year through September 2025. The Federal Reserve’s target for headline PCE inflation is 2%. Risks to the Outlook Looking ahead to the next few quarters, the outlook for the U.S. economy is favorable and economists view the risk of a recession as low. According to The Wall Street Journal’s survey of economists in October, the average probability of a recession in the next 12 months was just 24%, little changed from 25% in the July survey. The survey also indicated an improved near-term outlook. Projected real GDP growth in 2026 was revised up by 0.3 percentage points to 2.4%, and the expected unemployment rate in December 2026 was revised down to 4.2%. Compared with the July survey, respondents projected slightly higher headline inflation, lower core inflation, and higher interest rates. Energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty: Geopolitical uncertainty remains a risk to the medium-term inflation outlook. Energy prices are among the most volatile categories of inflation and reflect this uncertainty. Indeed, the energy goods and services CPI fell 1.5% in July but rebounded 2.1% in August and 5.2% in September. The timing, duration, and magnitude of energy price swings contribute to the risk of increased inflation in other goods and services – such as food (through fertilizer and fuel for farming equipment) and airfares – adding uncertainty to the medium-term inflation outlook. Importantly, the Trump Administration’s policies have made the U.S. economy more resilient to fluctuations in global oil prices. This resilience is due to a wide range of policies enacted, including deregulatory actions that have increased production and exports of oil and gas, and strategic actions abroad that have resulted in increased demand for U.S. crude and increased supply to the U.S. outside of the Middle East. Average domestic crude oil production in 2025 rose by 350,000 barrels per day relative to the 2024 average, and production and exports have risen further in 2026 as U.S. producers continue to build out U.S. infrastructure. The United States is increasingly the world’s largest producer of petroleum products and natural gas, and it is a net exporter of both. Business fixed investment and the manufacturing outlook: Recent data suggest that the economy is in the early stages of a policy-driven capital-expenditure boom. Since the passage of the Administration’s signature tax bill (the Working Families Tax Cuts), real BFI has risen by a cumulative 9.4% through 3Q26.  Provisions in the tax law – such as full expensing of research and development, 100% bonus depreciation for business equipment investments, and restoring deductibility of interest expenses for capital-intensive manufacturers – have contributed to this rapid business investment growth. Indeed, business equipment investment alone has added 0.8 percentage points to GDP growth over the past four quarters, while spending on intellectual property products has contributed 0.5 percentage points. The tax law also included a temporary provision for full depreciation deduction for the costs of new, nonresidential manufacturing facilities. Although real investment in factories and manufacturing structures has declined since mid-2024, the manufacturing outlook appears favorable. Jobs related to the construction of nonresidential buildings have grown by 116,000 since September 2025, presaging future manufacturing sector growth as new facilities are completed and products are deployed. In addition, firms that manufacture durable goods have increased their payrolls by 101,000 so far this year. Job openings in durable goods manufacturing grew by 93,000, and layoffs and discharges fell by 7,000. This capital expenditures boom bodes well for future economic growth. Capital expenditures correlate with productivity growth, which is a strategic pillar of the Administration’s economic agenda: productivity growth helps drive stronger economic growth and, as a positive supply-side development, is usually disinflationary while increasing wage growth. Interest rates: At the end of 2025, the yield on the 10-year Treasury note was 4.18%. As of October 30, it was 76 basis points higher. Several factors may have contributed to this increase, including optimism around U.S. growth expectations alongside higher demand for capital from investments related to SI. Since last year, economists’ forecasts have improved: the Blue Chip consensus for real GDP growth five years ahead has increased from 1.9% in the October 2025 report to 2.1% in the October 2026 report. Improved growth prospects can lead to higher interest rates as the returns from business investment rise. Increased demand for credit to finance capital investment also correlates with higher interest rates. The risk to the economic outlook is that higher borrowing costs could worsen the federal debt trajectory. However, U.S. fiscal sustainability does not appear to be a significant driver of the year-to-date increase in interest rates. Rate increases have been a global phenomenon even among countries with lower debt-to-GDP ratios. Super intelligence (SI): Investment in super intelligence has been a significant driver of economic growth in recent quarters. In the first three quarters of 2026, SI-driven investment (BFI in software, computers and hardware, and data center structures relative to pre-large language models trend) accounted for nearly 30% of GDP growth. In the long run, firms’ continued investment in super intelligence is likely to lead to efficiency gains, particularly in service-sector industries where productivity growth has been slower. However, the timeline and magnitude of productivity gains are uncertain, as is the ultimate effect on the composition of labor markets. If the integration of super intelligence acts as a standard technology improvement, productivity growth could return to historical norms after a period of above-trend growth. On the other hand, super intelligence could prove transformational and permanently upshift the path of productivity as it enables workers to build skills and human capital faster than in the past. Labor markets: While labor markets are in balance, labor data indicate an environment of lower job churn than in the past, which could leave the economy with less slack to absorb a negative shock. So far this year, the median private-sector hires rate has been 3.6%, compared to a median of 4.2% in 2019. By contrast, rates of layoffs and discharges for the private sector have remained near historical lows, with the layoffs rate at just 1.2% in August. The lower turnover environment, while indicating that labor markets are in balance, also suggests a large shock could shift markets out of balance as hiring may not be able to offset an increase in the layoffs and discharges rates. Conclusion The U.S. economy remains resilient, and the outlook is favorable. Historically high capital expenditures and steady household consumption growth have increased the economy’s capacity for self-sustaining growth. In the labor market, the unemployment rate and layoffs are low, wages are increasing, and new business applications hit an all-time high. Although energy markets have affected headline inflation, the U.S. economy is resilient to fluctuations in the supply of oil from the Strait of Hormuz, and energy prices should recede following the cessation of conflict in Iran. The Trump Administration has successfully stewarded major fiscal legislation to prevent a historic tax increase and lower the cost of capital, which has increased return expectations in the market. Since its passage in July 2025, we have seen significant business equipment investment, including industrial equipment. Indeed, current macroeconomic conditions bode well for increasing economic growth as the private sector leads. A net 22% of small businesses report plans to make capital outlays over the next six months, and the Business Roundtable reports that its index of CEO expectations of capital expenditures is now at its highest level since early 2022. Announced investments in U.S. manufacturing, production, and innovation total trillions of dollars, reflecting global confidence in the United States as a destination for investment. This capital expenditure boom is made possible by the Administration’s policies allowing full expensing of equipment and R&D, tariffs and reshoring incentives, and deregulation. The combined policies of the Trump Administration, both enacted and planned, provide a solid foundation for economic growth and will bring prosperity to all Americans. title: November 2, 2026 - FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality
body: FDA News Release FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality FDA issues final guidance for cell and gene therapy manufacturers, recommends building potency assurance into every stage of a therapy’s lifecycle — from early development through patient delivery For Immediate Release: November 02, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today issued final guidance for manufacturers of cellular and gene therapy (CGT) products to implement a comprehensive, science- and risk-based plan for making sure their products meet potency standards. The guidance provides FDA’s recommendations for a Potency Assurance Strategy, which guides manufacturers to test and verify — before a product reaches a patient — that every batch meets a defined standard of potency to do what the product is supposed to do therapeutically. The Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products final guidance replaces FDA's 2011 potency testing guidance for CGT products and applies to treatments for serious and often life-threatening conditions. By law, manufacturers are expected to verify that their products work as intended, from the time of approval through post-approval monitoring. This final guidance provides FDA’s current thinking and recommendations on how manufacturers can meet that requirement. "Patients who receive cellular and gene therapies are often battling serious or life-threatening conditions, such as cancers and rare diseases, and they deserve the assurance that the product administered to them will perform as intended," said Karim Mikhail, B. Pharm., M.S., Director of the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research . "This guidance reflects the FDA's commitment to ensuring America remains the best place in the world to innovate — and that innovation is matched by the highest standards of product quality and patient safety." The guidance provides flexible, risk-based recommendations for manufacturers on how to integrate potency considerations at every stage of development and commercialization — from early-phase investigational new drug (IND) submissions through biologics license application (BLA) approval and continued post-market verification. Key topics include controls for variability in raw materials, testing during manufacturing, and lab tests that confirm each batch is biologically active in a way that matches its intended therapeutic effect. The guidance also addresses specialized considerations for products with short shelf lives, viral vector gene therapies, and patient-specific therapies. By giving manufacturers a clear, predictable roadmap, this guidance supports faster access to safe and effective therapies for patients who often have no other treatment options — many of whom receive products made individually for a single person. In doing so, it advances the FDA's public health pillars: protecting patients through rigorous quality standards, promoting innovation by providing regulatory clarity, and reinforcing the integrity of the supply chain for some of the most complex medical products in existence. The FDA will host a webinar on December 10, 2026, to help stakeholders understand and implement the guidance. Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

Teams across Google are working on ways to unlock AI’s benefits in fields as wide-ranging as healthcare, crisis response, and education. To keep you posted on our progress, we're doing a regular roundup of Google's most recent AI news. Here’s a look back at some of our AI announcements from October. October underscored our commitment to AI innovation, as we released one frontier model globally and announced our next one just two weeks later. After rolling out Gemini 4 Argon — a frontier reasoning model — to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers, we announced Gemini 4 Carbon , our strongest model yet for long-horizon engineering and cybersecurity defense. Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward while strengthening our safety guardrails in tandem. Elsewhere in October, we introduced Genie 4 for real-time interactive world simulation with native audio, unveiled our smartest fitness tracker with Google Fitbit Edge , broke open a 20-year bottleneck in quantum computing , and more. Put Gemini 4 Argon to work today, and see what’s next for Gemini 4 at the frontier . Following early safety testing, Gemini 4 Argon rolled out globally for complex coding, financial analysis, and legal workflows across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Google Cloud, Search, and the Gemini app , while also powering physical-world reasoning through Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics . Showing how quickly we’re pushing the frontier forward, two weeks later we announced Gemini 4 Carbon , our strongest model yet with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. Just as we did with Argon, we’re taking a deliberate approach to rollout: Carbon is now in pre-release testing with the U.S. government and a subset of trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program as we refine safety guardrails and expand partner testing ahead of a broader launch to developers, businesses, and consumers. Step into real-time interactive worlds with Genie 4 . Genie 4 brings unprecedented realism, advanced physics, lifelike human movement, and native audio to real-time interactive simulation. You can steer scenes as they unfold using natural language. Genie 4 advances on our ability to create safe training environments for robots and AI agents as a crucial step toward AGI. Explore the demos on the Google DeepMind blog . Verify AI-generated content more easily around the world . Having already watermarked more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio with SynthID, we’re expanding SynthID Detector globally in English so anyone can check whether an image, video, or audio clip was generated with AI. Alongside built-in verification tools in Search, Chrome, and the Gemini app that regularly handle over a million requests each day, SynthID Detector also identifies AI content from industry partners like OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao, and Apple. Stay protected from mobile scams with new Android safeguards . AI-powered Scam Detection in Phone by Google and Google Messages already flags more than 5 million suspected scam calls and texts every month. Now, Android is introducing an opt-in Enhanced protection mode in Google Messages that uses Private AI Compute and our latest cloud Gemini models to catch sophisticated conversational scams, paired with expanded chat alerts and stronger call-forwarding and screen-sharing defenses. See how AI could improve patient-physician relationships in clinical care . In Google’s first publication in the main journal of The Lancet , researchers from Google and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center evaluated our AMIE conversational medical AI system during real-world primary care clinic visits. By gathering patient histories and generating clinical summaries before urgent care appointments , AMIE helped clinicians prepare in 75% of cases and matched doctors’ final differential diagnoses 90% of the time. This is part of our broader work applying AI to better understand, detect, and treat disease . Create and play custom games in Playground . Our new experimental gaming platform lets anyone build, remix, and share custom single- and multiplayer games from simple text prompts with zero coding required. That same no-code creativity is expanding across our platforms: Android users can now build personal AI apps with Google AI Studio and install them directly on their phones through Google Play , and music producers can vibe code custom instruments and audio plugins in Google Flow Music . Celebrate educators and sharpen your learning . For World Teachers’ Day, teachers from around the globe shared how they use Gemini to personalize lessons and spark critical thinking, alongside a new global idea search launched in partnership with TED. Whether you’re in the classroom or preparing for a big project, you can also study smarter with Gemini Notebook using interactive learning overviews and custom quizzes, and use new co-creation controls to shape your Slide Decks and Video Overviews before they generate. Engineered on the Gemma 4 architecture with 740 million parameters, our new open embedding model moves beyond text to map code, images, video, and audio into a single unified space right on everyday devices. Its modular design cuts local vector storage by up to 6x, making it easy for developers to build private, offline apps that can find a specific video clip from a voice memo or search hours of audio with a text query. Read the first AI response beamed back from our Project Suncatcher satellite . After launching TPUs into low-Earth orbit , our first Project Suncatcher prototype satellite returned the first-ever AI response generated by a data center-class Google TPU in space: a haiku composed onboard by Gemma 4. This milestone confirms our hardware survived launch and can run AI workloads in orbit.
